title: Astrid and the Autopsy
premise: Sebastian Ashgrove, the concierge at the Marlowe Grand, has spent two decades cataloguing the town of Bellhaven's secrets in a private ledger—until twin letters arrive after the death of matriarch Vivienne Crane: one confessing to the drowning of Vivienne's daughter twenty years ago, one promising Sebastian 'the inheritance you were owed.' Following the letters' clues, Sebastian discovers she is Vivienne's unacknowledged granddaughter and that her own mother was framed for the death. The killer is the town's beloved coroner, Dr. Ilsa Renner, who staged the original autopsy; Sebastian corners her with the ledger's evidence and the coroner's second confession letter, clearing her mother's name but choosing to keep her inheritance secret to protect her found family at the hotel.
about_author: Ansel Villalobos is a former night-shift hotel clerk who swears half his debut novel came from real guest ledgers he probably shouldn't have read. He writes mysteries about people who see everything and are seen by no one.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet the concierge mid-shift, watching guests lie beautifully, and learn of her private ledger of Bellhaven's secrets. News breaks that reclusive heiress Vivienne Crane has died. Emotional beat: quiet pride in invisibility, undercut by loneliness.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A lawyer delivers two letters posthumously sent by Vivienne: one confessing to her daughter Lark's drowning, one promising Sebastian an inheritance 'you were owed since the night your mother ran.' Shock: her mother's flight connects to the case. Beat: vertigo as her ordered life cracks open.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Never Held
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with flashbacks. She searches her twenty years of entries for Lark Crane and finds a page deliberately torn out—one she doesn't remember removing. Someone has been inside her ledger. Beat: paranoia; the watcher realizes she is watched.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Kind Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Dr. Ilsa Renner, who signed Lark's autopsy and now gently warns Sebastian off 'reopening old wounds.' Sebastian notes the doctor's too-perfect recall of details never made public. Beat: charm on the surface, threat beneath.

chapters.title: Room 412 Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Hotel staff POV (Marta, the housekeeper). The staff—the family Sebastian never admitted to having—reveal they've long protected her, including hiding a guest connected to Lark's death years ago. Beat: warmth and guilt; found family has been holding her up unseen.

chapters.title: A Drowning Without Water
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She obtains the original autopsy file and finds the impossible detail: Lark drowned in river water though she died miles inland. The confession letter's timeline contradicts it. Beat: cold clarity—the confession is false, engineered to misdirect.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Lawyer's office scene, Sebastian's POV. The will names her heir only if she publicly accepts the confession as truth. Refuse, and everything goes to a trust controlled by Dr. Renner. Beat: fury and temptation; the trap is priced exactly to her needs.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Reconstructing the torn ledger page from memory and Marta's testimony, she proves Renner falsified the autopsy to protect Vivienne's husband—and later killed Vivienne when she tried to confess. Renner realizes what Sebastian knows. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Last Check-Out
chapters.summary: Climax, Sebastian's POV. Renner comes to the Marlowe Grand at closing time to retrieve the ledger. In the empty lobby, Sebastian stalls her while Marta alerts the sheriff, using the hotel itself—keys, cameras, the register—as a weapon. Beat: terror transmuted into command.

chapters.title: Everything in Its Place
chapters.summary: Resolution, Sebastian's POV. Renner confesses; Sebastian's mother is exonerated posthumously. Sebastian declines the public inheritance, keeping her name out of papers, and adds a final entry to the ledger—not a sin this time, but her own name, finally written down. Beat: belonging without exposure.
